title: Phase 1 transaction assumption not enforced in update_delivery_state
description:
What: update_delivery_state() and update_read_at() perform the data UPDATE outside a transaction, then wrap only the state counter increment in a second transaction. The code explicitly comments (lines 275-278) that this is safe 'because Phase 1 is single-threaded.' This constraint is not enforced at compile time or checked at runtime.

Why: If Phase 2 introduces concurrent writers (multi-device sync, cross-device updates), the two-transaction approach becomes a consistency bug. A message UPDATE succeeds, then the process crashes before the counter transaction commits. Result: message exists but state token is stale, and clients miss the change event. Test suite has no verification that counter increments are atomic with message updates.

How to apply: (1) Wrap both the message UPDATE and the counter increment in a single transaction, or (2) add a prominent runtime check that panics if called from an async context (Phase 2 guard). Document the Phase 1 assumption prominently. Add an integration test that verifies state_version is always incremented when delivery_state changes.
